summary: Intermittent 429s and missing throttle headers after subaccount split: SSE keepalives vs webhook callbacks consuming burst credits
description:
Issue summary:
BrightVoice reports intermittent 429s immediately after a subaccount split/tenant reparenting. The pattern: long-lived SSE connections (keepalive pings every 30s) experience opaque 429s with no X-RateLimit headers, while a burst of webhook callbacks (signed URL POSTs) succeed concurrently.

Impact:
- Production user-facing chat widgets intermittently drop streaming updates for ~5-20s.
- Retry loops on the client escalate CPU and duplicate webhook deliveries.
- Observed by multiple BrightVoice accounts in the same dedicated GPU pool.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (dedicated-02), prod-us-west.
- Subaccount split performed 2026-03-09 22:10 UTC (BrightVoice initiated migrate-subaccounts v2).
- SSE connections established from browser clients via api-edge (http/2 -> origin).

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Run a large webhook fanout (200 concurrent signed-URL callbacks) to the same tenant after triggering the subaccount split.
2) Keep ~150 active SSE clients connected and emitting keepalives every 30s.
3) Observe sporadic 429s on SSE connections (no rate-limit headers) while webhook callbacks mostly succeed.

Observed behavior:
- SSE responses are rejected with 429 and connection reset. Client logs show no X-RateLimit-* headers.
- Server-side ingress metrics show a temporary drop in available burst credits for that tenant immediately after the split.
- Console shows route-level token counters not decreasing for webhook route (route reports normal usage) but tenant-level burst credit decremented.

Expected behavior:
- Long-lived SSE keepalives should be accounted against a separate long-lived/session pool or at least expose clear throttle headers telling client retry window.
- Webhook callbacks and SSE keepalives should not silently steal each other's burst credit in a way that produces opaque 429s.

Logs / trace identifiers provided by customer:
- TraceIDs: trace-20260310-3a7f, trace-20260310-3a8c
- Example client timestamp: 2026-03-09T22:27:14.523Z
- Customer attached packet captures and server-side sample logs (sse_connection_id=sv-7f2d).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Acknowledge receipt. Escalating to SRE/edge team. Asked for exact migration command and any custom ingress proxies.

2026-03-10 10:03 - Liam Chen (SRE): Confirmed dedicated pool and noted similar ticket SUP-246824 mentioned refill misalignment after tenant reparenting. Will pull rate-limiter debug logs for affected tenant-id.
2026-03-10 12:45 - BrightVoice Tech (customer): Provided curl samples, packet captures and the migration log. Says they saw 429s persist for ~18 minutes then subside.

2026-03-11 07:30 - Liam Chen (SRE): Found a window where edge-proxy health checks caused double-accounting against tenant burst during reparent event. Still validating whether SSE keepalives were scored against a short-window burst pool.

2026-03-12 15:02 - Elena Ruiz (Platform Eng): Reproduced a similar pattern in staging using tenant-split simulator. Drafted a candidate fix to isolate long-lived connection keepalives into an exemption pool with explicit header reporting.
investigation_notes: Checked rate-limiter logs for tenant 'brightvoice-44' between 2026-03-09T22:05 and 2026-03-09T22:40. Observed a refill event where origin and edge both applied a partial refill, but the handoff left the tenant with an unexpectedly low effective burst budget.
Edge-proxy (http2) triggered connection reuse behavior: SSE keepalive frames were mapped to a generic /events path which shares token accounting with signed-url callbacks (POST /cb).

Observed lack of X-RateLimit headers for SSE rejections because the edge rejects early at the token-bucket layer (pre-auth) and the header propagation path is bypassed when reject happens in the pre-routing layer.

Staging reproduce: tenant-split flow + concurrent webhook burst + 150 simulated SSE keepalives -> SSE 429s observed. When we moved SSE keepalive to use a distinct client-id header, accounting separated and 429s stopped.

Hypothesis: tenant-split causes a short-lived mismatch in burst-credit ownership between edge and origin. Because SSE and webhook use different route selectors but same token bucket, the transient low-burst state results in opaque SSE 429s with header-less rejects.
resolution:
Workaround implemented: temporary config change applied to dedicated-02 to grant 'long-lived-connection' exemption pool for BrightVoice for 24 hours and enabled verbose throttle headers on pre-routing rejects. Customer verified streaming recovery after change.

Planned fix: engineering will land the following in next sprint (PR linked):
- Isolate long-lived SSE/WS keepalive traffic into a distinct refill bucket at the edge so route-level and session-level traffic do not compete for the same burst credits. (Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/498).
- Ensure pre-routing rejects include X-RateLimit headers by plumbing header emission into the token-bucket reject path.

Follow-ups and action items:
- Postmortem note: schedule after next week to capture incident timeline and recommend tenant-split runbook additions. (Owner: Elena Ruiz).
- Add an automated check in the migration playbook to verify tenant burst credit parity between edge and origin before cutover. (Owner: Platform SRE).
- CS to follow up with BrightVoice on 2026-03-15 to confirm no recurrence and communicate planned fix timeline.

Status: Mitigated (temporary exemption applied). Engineering work in-progress for permanent fix.
